rounds.text: Inspire Films Ltd is heavily under-appreciated because its asset backing offers deep value, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.47x against a sector benchmark of 1.21x [E7], with the stock priced at ₹ 9.50 on a book value of ₹ 20.2 [E2]. Momentum is also building as earnings growth accelerates [E63] alongside YoY profit growth exceeding 20% [E61]. Efficiency metrics further bolster the bull case, with an ROA of 0% outperforming the sector benchmark of -9.58% [E8], and a ROCE of 2.87% that beats the sector benchmark of 1.47% [E10]. Conceded: the 5-year compounded sales growth is -12% [E14], 3-year compounded sales growth is -41% [E15], and median return on equity over 3 years stands at -3% [E22].

Inspire Films Ltd exhibits a severe structural contraction in its top line, highlighted by a compounded sales growth of -12% over 5 years and an even steeper collapse of -41% over 3 years [E14, E15], alongside a recent screen flag of sales down -65% YoY [E64]. This chronic revenue decay is paired with persistently anaemic profitability, demonstrated by a 5-year median return on equity of just 2% and a negative 3% median ROE over 3 years [E21, E22], cementing the official flag for low ROE over the last three years [E57]. Despite these dismal foundational returns, the stock trades at an unjustifiable P/E of 35.19x, representing a massive premium over the sector benchmark of 18.38x [E6]. Compounding these equity risks, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4] and sits depressed at only 17% of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months is 31% [E16] and ROCE of 2.87% beats the sector benchmark ROCE of 1.47% [E10].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 and 5 years is -41% and -12% respectively [E14, E15], and the bear is correct about the low ROE flags [E57, E65]. However, the bear ignores the dramatic inflection in the top line where compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has rebounded to 31% [E16], invalidating a purely static view of revenue decay. Furthermore, profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 164% because earnings growth is actively accelerating, which triggered explicit positive screens for YoY profit growth above 20% [E51, E61, E63]. While the bear focuses on absolute valuation multiples, it omits the profound asset-value protection provided by a price-to-book ratio of 0.47x, trading at a steep discount to the sector benchmark of 1.21x [E7]. Finally, the company's ROCE of 2.87% actually outperforms the sector benchmark of 1.47% [E10], and its return on assets sits at 0% against a deeply negative sector benchmark of -9.58% [E8].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has rebounded to 31% [E16]. However, this single-period bounce does not erase a multi-year contraction characterized by a 3-year sales decline of -41% [E15], a 5-year sales decay of -12% [E14], and a severe recent quarterly sales drop of -65% YoY [E64]. The bull points to asset protection via a price-to-book ratio of 0.47x [E7], but ignores that this low valuation is justified by a 5-year median return on equity of just 2% [E21], a 3-year median ROE of -3% [E22], and a last-year ROE stuck at 1% [E23, E65]. While the bull highlights an ROCE of 2.87% [E10], that figure is still anemic in absolute terms and falls well below the sector median ROCE of 5.6% [E72]. Finally, the claimed earnings acceleration overlooks the broader fundamental drag of a poor 5-year sales growth record [E56] and a negative 3-year return on equity of -2.61% [E57].
